name: India–Pakistan
value: Airspace bans in force to 24 Dec
summary: Pakistan extends its airspace ban on Indian aircraft to 24 Dec; no cross-border strike or mobilisation found
state: Pakistan extended its ban on Indian-registered and Indian-operated aircraft, including military flights, to 24 Dec in a NOTAM reported on 19 Nov; both countries have barred each other's airlines since April 2025, after the Pahalgam attack (Dawn). Air India puts the annual cost of the closure at about $455 million. Searches to 25 Nov found no cross-border strike or mobilisation, so Watch holds on the continuing bilateral suspensions.
for_you: Flights between Europe and India may take longer routes while Pakistani airspace stays closed to Indian airlines. Travellers to Kashmir and border areas can check FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Watch: bilateral suspensions since April 2025 persist (airspace bans extended to 24 Dec); no cross-border strikes or mobilisation

sources.title: Dawn — Airspace ban on Indian aircraft extended till Dec 24

why: Two nuclear-armed neighbours with a history of rapid escalation after terrorist attacks.
drivers: Kashmir attacks, Line of Control firing, water disputes (Indus), domestic politics.

rubric.watch: Ceasefire violations, a major terrorist attack with blame assigned, or treaty suspensions.
rubric.normal: Ceasefire holding along the Line of Control; no major attacks.
